$comment: The connectors Sherman knows how to reach — MCP servers and credentialed
APIs — declared as data so the launcher can render engine config without
knowing any connector by name.
This file is the CATALOG: what exists, how it launches, what it needs, and
where a human gets the credential when one is required. It is committed.
Enablement and secrets are NOT here. They live at ~/.sherman/connectors.json
on each machine, chmod 600, never committed and never synced. See
docs/CONNECTORS.md.
It carries capabilities.json's rule, for the same reason: an entry describes
a connector that really exists and really launches this way. A speculative
entry is not a roadmap item here — it is engine config that fails at
startup, which the operator meets as one causeless error far from its cause.
The `0-1` skill is what adds entries, and it is required to verify before
it writes.
Fields:
name               stable id; becomes the MCP server name in both engines
summary            one lowercase phrase, what it gives Sherman
transport          'stdio' | 'http'
commandCandidates  stdio: absolute paths tried in order; first executable
one wins. A list, not a string, because a Python venv
is bin/python on Unix and Scripts/python.exe on Windows
and that difference is not worth a branch in the caller.
args               stdio: argv after the command
url, headers       http: endpoint and headers
requiresFile       paths that must exist for the connector to be installed
probe              argv appended to the resolved command; must exit 0 or
the connector is treated as present-but-broken. Files
existing is not an install: a venv whose packages never
installed passes every existence check and then hands
the engine a server that dies on startup.
requires           secret NAMES this connector cannot run without
autoEnable         true when the connector needs no credential and its
probe is a sufficient gate; it wires itself once
installed. Everything else waits for an entry in the
machine's enablement file.
repair             what to run when the probe fails
signup             { url, what } — where a human gets the credential and
what to ask for. This is what 0-1 reads when it has to
hand over a checklist instead of wiring silently.
${SHERMAN_HOME} and ${HOME} expand at render time. No other substitution
happens: a placeholder that does not resolve blocks the connector rather
than rendering a literal ${...} into engine config.

connectors.name: llmwiki
connectors.summary: your personal research wiki, searched and written over MCP
